title: Procurement Fastlane: SOC2 assertion pack + insurance flexibility experiments
creator: Maya Patel
description: Run a set of pricing and packaging experiments to reduce enterprise procurement friction by building a 'fastlane' onboarding flow. The experiment combines a pre-packaged SOC2 assertion bundle (attestation artifacts, scope matrix, shared evidence links) with modular insurance options and templated contract clauses. Goal: shorten legal/procurement decision time, increase self-serve conversions for mid-market and lower-touch enterprise customers, and quantify risk surface for new simplified packages.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver SOC2 assertion pack template that legal and security approve for reuse
Create 2 insurance SKU options with underwriting thresholds and optional broker flow
Implement prototype vendor-portal flow that auto-populates contract appendix and evidence links
Run pilot with 3 sales accounts and measure time-to-contract, procurement touchpoints, and win-rate delta
updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff with Legal, Security, Sales Engineering, and Growth. Agreed scope: public SOC2 summary + scannable evidence index; no claims on scope beyond assertion package.
2026-01-25: Security provided acceptable SOC2 artifact list and redaction guidance. Trade-off noted: redacting context increases TOC rework for procurement.
2026-02-08: Design created vendor-portal mock that pre-fills 'assurance appendix' using customer metadata (region, data residency). Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/PROC/fastlane-prototype
2026-02-21: Insurance team proposed two paths: (A) fixed-premium add-on for lower exposures, (B) broker-assisted dynamic quote for enterprise. Decided to A/B test both.

2026-03-03: Engineering spike (ENG-4321) for PDF assembly and signed artifact generation is 60% complete; blocker: HSM integration for artifact stamping. Mitigation: use temp signed metadata until HSM rollout.
2026-03-10: Sales pilot recruits: Acme Health (mid-market), Nimbus Analytics (enterprise), and Tradewing (mid-market). Expected pilot start 2026-03-20.

2026-03-12: Legal reviewed the initial contract appendix. Feedback: clarify indemnity carveouts and retention periods. Action assigned to Diego to update templates and re-run security review. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/218
risks_and_tradeoffs: Simplifying SOC2 artifacts may increase procurement follow-ups if redactions are insufficient
Fixed-premium insurance may underprice tail risk for high-exposure customers, requiring manual escalation
Bundling assurances could reduce negotiation time but may reduce revenue from bespoke legal consulting fees
measurement_plan: Primary metric: median time from NDA/LOI to signed MSA (target: -30% vs baseline)
Secondary metrics: number of procurement Q&A rounds, legal review cycles per account, pilot win-rate vs matched historical cohort
Instrumentation: tag contract templates in CRM, add 'procurement_flow' event in Console onboarding funnel
next_steps: Finish engineering spike for artifact generation and HSM fallback by 2026-03-18
Update contract appendix per Legal feedback and submit for final security review by 2026-03-19
Launch pilot flows with three accounts starting 2026-03-20 and stand up weekly metrics dashboard
Prepare Customer Success playbook for guided self-serve procurement conversations
